analysis_corrected: The conclusion first written here ('network reputation; only a different egress or the keyed API would return results') is withdrawn. Follow-up controls on the same public address showed the 403 is query-keyed: the homepage returns 200, ordinary queries return the solvable 200 ALTCHA wall, the shipped client returns real results, and changing the user agent and client hints changes nothing. See mojeek-403-mechanism-controls.json.
conclusion: The 403 is a hard, per-query automated-query refusal, not parser drift and not a solvable challenge. It is not a network-wide or user-agent-wide block.
